project_name: Contra Costa 230 kV Line Terminals Reconfiguration
brief_description: Swap Lone Tree – Contra Costa PP 230 kV line and Birds Landing – Contra Costa PP 230 kV line terminal positions at Contra Costa PP 230 kV Substation and relocate Windmaster from Section F to Section E.
objectives: Protects against the NERC TPL-001-4 Category P2 bus tie breaker fault at Contra Costa PP 230 kV bus. Las Positas – Newark 230 kV line was overloaded following a P2-4 contingency starting in 20
driver_detail: Category P2 bus tie breaker fault causes overload on Las Positas-Newark 230 kV line starting 2023. Current bus configuration at Contra Costa PP 230 kV substation concentrates load on single paths under P2 contingency. Project swaps terminal positions of Lone Tree–Contra Costa and Birds Landing–Contra Costa 230 kV lines and relocates Windmaster. This eliminates the bus configuration bottleneck. The issue is a structural bus configuration deficiency, not load growth.
alternatives_rejected: • • Converting to BAAH Add sectionalizing breaker not recommended as the fourth section would be beyond PG&E’s standard. March 17, 2022

project_name: Vasona-Metcalf 230 kV Line Limiting Elements Removal Project
brief_description: The scope of this project is to remove the limiting elements for Vasona-Metcalf 230 kV line at Vasona and Metcalf Substations to achieve the line conductor rating
objectives: Upgrade terminal equipment rating to achieve full conductor capacity
need_date: NERC Category P2 and P7 starting 2023.
driver_detail: Terminal equipment (wave traps and associated conductors) at Vasona and Metcalf substations are rated below the Vasona-Metcalf 230 kV line conductor's full capacity. P2 and P7 contingency overloads identified starting 2023. Project removes these limiting elements to achieve the full line conductor rating. The issue is a terminal equipment rating gap, not load growth. Alternative 152 MW×4h energy storage rejected as not cost-effective.
alternatives_rejected: • Energy storage, which is not recommended because a roughly 152 MW*4 hour energy storage will be required to mitigate all the identified overloads and it will not be cost-effective. March 17, 2022

brief_description: Reconductor Borden-Cassidy and Cassidy-Coppermine and add voltage support at Coppemine
objectives: Prevent normal overlads and low voltages at coppermine
need_date: P0 overloads based on historical data
driver_detail: Three concurrent drivers: (1) P0 overloads on Borden-Cassidy and Cassidy-Coppermine 70 kV lines confirmed in historical/real-time operations (equip_aging); (2) future local demand growth in the Coppermine area compounds the overloads (load_growth); (3) low voltage issues at Coppermine 70 kV bus accompany the thermal overloads (voltage). Project reconductors both line segments and adds voltage support at Coppermine. Interim operational measure (normal-open Tivy Valley CB 42) cannot address long-term need.
load_growth_evidence: Project need date is 'P0 overloads based on historical data' with future local demand growth in the area driving the need for permanent reinforcement beyond the temporary operational measure.
alternatives_rejected: • • Introduction of 115 kV source as its not cost-effective Energy Storage is not recommended as it will also trigger a complete 70 kV bus upgrade which is expensive. Other alternative interconnection optionsa are not feasible. March 17, 2022
interim_solution: Tivy Valley CB 42 to be normal open in summer to prevent overloads and low voltages

brief_description: The scope of this project is to replace the Cortina 230/115/60 kV Bank #1 with one 230/115 kV and one 115/60 kV transformer banks
objectives: Thermal overload issues for Cortina 230/115/60 kV Bank #1 for NERC Category P1 and P3 contingencies
driver_detail: Category P1 and P3 contingency overloads on Cortina 230/115/60 kV Bank #1 starting 2023. Under loss of the parallel bank, Bank #1 is overloaded because it cannot serve the combined load alone. Replacing the three-winding transformer with separate 230/115 kV and 115/60 kV transformer banks removes the physical bottleneck. The three alternatives that were rejected (operational reliance, converting bank, or adding new bank) were more expensive. The overload is a structural capacity deficiency, not load growth.

Converting Existing Cortina 230/115/60 kV Bank #1 to 115/60 kV and adding one new 230/115 kV. The cos is higher than the proposed project ($25M - $50M) Keeping existing Cortina 230/115/60 kV bank #1 and add one new 230/115 kV bank. The cost is higher than the proposed project ($22M $44M) March 17, 2022

brief_description: Reconductor 2.4 miles between Manteca and Ripon Jct and 1.8 miles between Riverbank SW STA and Valley Home Tap.
objectives: Reconductor Manteca - Ripon Jct - Valley Home Tap
driver_detail: Category P1 contingency overloads starting 2023 on short bottleneck sections: 2.4 miles between Manteca and Ripon Jct, and 1.8 miles between Riverbank SW STA and Valley Home Tap. These sections have ratings below the conductor's full capacity. Line re-rate alternative was rejected because the re-rate applies only until 7pm whereas the area peak load occurs after 7pm, confirming that the conductor itself is the physical limiting element rather than a temporary operational constraint.
alternatives_rejected: • Line Re-rate: This is not applicable in the area as the re-rate is only up to 7pm while the peak load in the area occurs after 7pm. March 17, 2022
interim_solution: Operating measure to connect Ripon load as a tap to the 115 kV line

brief_description: To build two HVDC lines, 1) from Newark 230 kV to NRS 230 kV and 2) Metcalf 500 kV to San Jose B 115 kV.
objectives: To address multiple category contingencies driven near, mid and long-term reliability issues in San Jose 115 kV system.
driver_detail: Approximately 500 MW (~75%) load increase in the Silicon Valley Power (SVP) service area is the primary driver. Forecasted near-, mid-, and long-term load growth exceeds the capacity of the existing 115 kV system and makes conventional 115 kV reconductoring insufficient. New 230 kV AC alternatives were rejected because of unbalanced natural flows from Newark and Metcalf sources. Energy storage rejected because San Jose system has far less charging capacity than required. Two HVDC lines (Newark 230–NRS 230 and Metcalf 500–San Jose B 115) provide controlled power transfer proportional to the scale of load growth.
load_growth_evidence: Report explicitly states the forecasted overall San Jose area load is beyond the capacity of 115 kV lines, with ~500 MW (~75%) load increase in SVP service area driving the need for entirely new transmission infrastructure.
alternatives_rejected: • 115 kV lines reconductoring: This alternative is not recommended as the forecasted overall San Jose area load is beyond capacity of 115 kV lines. New 230 kV AC lines from Newark and Metcalf: This alternative is not recommended because of unbalance in natural flows from the Newark and Metcalf sources. Energy Storage: This alternative is not recommended as previous studies have shown that San Jose system has far less charging capacity compared to the size of energy storage needed to address all reliability issues identified in the area. March 17, 2022
interim_solution: Operation soluiton and series compensation device for flow control.

project_name: Series Compensation on Los Esteros-Nortech 115 kV Line
brief_description: To install about 2 ohm series reactor on the Los Esteros-Nortech 115 kV line.
objectives: To address ctitical (P1 contengency driven) issue on the Los Esteros-Nortech 115 kV line in the interim.
driver_detail: Critical P1 contingency overload on the Los Esteros-Nortech 115 kV line driven by the same SVP area load growth that necessitates the San Jose Area HVDC Lines project. The series reactor (2 ohm) is the interim measure providing flow control while the HVDC project is constructed. Load growth in the San Jose/SVP area is the root cause of the overload. Project is time-limited (in-service 2023, same as need date) and planned to be superseded by the HVDC project.
load_growth_evidence: The series compensation is explicitly an interim solution for the SVP area load growth issue while the San Jose HVDC project is built. The same load growth (~500 MW, ~75% in SVP area) drives both projects.
alternatives_rejected: • 115 kV lines reconductoring: This alternative is not recommended due to higher cost. March 17, 2022

brief_description: The scope of this project is to install another 500/230 kV transformer bank at the Table Mountain substation.
objectives: There are high voltage issues in the Table Mountain/Palermo 230 kV area under the maintenance outage or contingency of the existing 500/230 kV transformer at Table Mountain substation. This project will address the issue.
driver_detail: High voltage issues in the Table Mountain/Palermo 230 kV area arise under maintenance outage or contingency of the existing 500/230 kV transformer. High voltage conditions are exacerbated by heavy renewable (solar/PV) output during light load periods, when the single transformer is insufficient to absorb excess reactive power. A second transformer bank provides additional reactive absorption capacity to control voltage. The renewable (high solar) operating environment is the context that makes the single-transformer contingency unmanageable without system additions.
alternatives_rejected: • • Do nothing (status quo) Install reactive support device March 17, 2022

brief_description: The scope of this project is to install a voltage regulator at the existing Atlantic 60 kV substation .
objectives: There are high voltage issues on the 60 kV system which is radially supplied by the Atlantic 230/60 kV transformer. The transformer does not have LTC and there are no means for operators to control the voltage. This project will address the issue.
driver_detail: High voltage issues on the 60 kV system radially supplied by the Atlantic 230/60 kV transformer. The transformer lacks a load tap changer (LTC), meaning operators have no direct means to control voltage on the 60 kV system. The voltage regulator provides the needed voltage control capability. This is a voltage control capability gap, not load growth or equipment aging — the transformer was never installed with LTC.
alternatives_rejected: • • Do nothing (status quo) Replace the transformer with another one with LTC March 17, 2022

brief_description: Convert two bus positions from the existing double bus double breaker configuration to breaker-and-a-half configuration by adding a tie breaker and relocate two lines.
objectives: Mitigate voltage instability risk during planned/unplanned Victor 230kV bus outage and associated constraints; provide operational flexibility and enhance reliability
driver_detail: Voltage instability risk during planned or unplanned Victor 230 kV bus outage. The existing double-bus double-breaker (DBDB) configuration at Victor 230 kV switchrack causes critical lines to be disconnected during a bus outage, creating a voltage collapse risk. Converting two bus positions to breaker-and-a-half (BAAH) configuration by adding a tie breaker and relocating 2 lines maintains line connectivity during bus outages and eliminates the voltage instability risk. Sole alternative ('status quo') was rejected due to the voltage instability risk.
alternatives_rejected: • Status Quo. This alternative is not recommended due to the post contingency voltage instability risk March 17, 2022

brief_description: Minor system reconfiguration needed, to avoid a system voltage collapse following loss of the remaining Devers 230 kV bus, during a planned outage of the other Devers 230 kV bus.
objectives: With one of the two 230 kV buses at the Devers substation de-energized for maintenance purposes; a fault on the second bus would result in a system voltage collapse. During this event, with the current bus configuration, the Devers - Mirage No. 2 and Devers - Vista No. 2 lines would be disconnected, from the Devers substation. This would result in voltage collapse for that area; and isolation of the IID and MWD systems from the SCE system. The proposed bus configuration, during the same event described above, the Devers - Mirage No. 2 line would stay connected to the system through the Devers 1AA Bank; while the Devers - Vista No. 2 line would serve the 4A Bank, and a system voltage collapse would be avoided.
driver_detail: With one of the two 230 kV buses at Devers de-energized for planned maintenance, a fault on the remaining bus disconnects both Devers-Mirage No. 2 and Devers-Vista No. 2 lines, causing voltage collapse for the area and isolating IID and MWD systems from the SCE system. The reconfigured bus keeps Devers-Mirage No. 2 connected through the 1AA Bank and Devers-Vista No. 2 serving the 4A Bank during the same event, preventing voltage collapse. Driver is voltage stability under maintenance outage condition.
alternatives_rejected: Do nothing March 17, 2022

project_name: Antelope 66 kV Short Circuit Duty Mitigation Project
brief_description: This project proposes to upgrade the existing Antelope 66 kV switchrack to a 50 kA short circuit duty rating by replacing (41) 66 kV circuit breakers, (101) 66 kV ground disconnect switches, (45) 66 kV potential transformers, performing a ground grid study, and removing (15) steel lattice structures and installing (15) new dead-end structures.
region: SCE Tehachapi and Big Creek Area
objectives: The existing circuit breakers are currently operating at 96 percent of their 40 kA short circuit duty rating and our preliminary analyses show that adding the CPUC portfolio generation at the Antelope Substation 230 kV bus alone will trigger the need for circuit breaker replacement.
driver_detail: Existing Antelope 66 kV circuit breakers are operating at 96% of their 40 kA short circuit duty rating, already near the equipment limit (equip_aging). Adding CPUC portfolio generation (renewable) at the Antelope 230 kV bus will increase fault current levels and push the breakers beyond their 40 kA rating, making replacement necessary (renewable). The project upgrades 41 circuit breakers, 101 ground disconnect switches, and 45 potential transformers to 50 kA rating. The 45-month upgrade timeline makes this the critical-path upgrade for new generation interconnection in the Tehachapi area.
alternatives_rejected: Do nothing March 17, 2022
